apps.subtitle: PlayStation 2 emulator for ARM64
apps.localizedDescription: A free and open-source PlayStation 2 (PS2) emulator based on PCSX2, with native ARM64 JIT recompilers. Play PS2 games on your phone, PC, or gaming handheld.

versions.localizedDescription:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- Android: graphics problem reports take a savestate by default
- Android: problem reports scrub the app's own /data paths
- Android: problem report takes the save state first and stops the game when the dump's frames are recorded
- GS dump: say where a requested dump is, so the caller can act when its frames are recorded
- Android: a crash report says which driver the crashed run actually opened
- Android: problem reports fill in the game's CRC
- Android: problem reports name the build's commit without the driver report
- Android: a crash report that fails to build keeps its Not sent line
- Android: crash startup work runs once per process
- Android: problem report screens go back a step, ask before deleting, and keep their work off the main thread
- Android: problem report capture takes the save state after the dump, refreshes the logs, and can be given up on
- Android: report uploads retry for real, wait for Wi-Fi, can be stopped and no longer trust the clock
- Android: ask about a crash only when one happened in front of the user
- Android: problem reports no longer carry the RetroAchievements user, network addresses or file:// paths
- Android: "Report a problem" flow, My reports, and their entry points
- Android: collect, arm the crash marker, and upload problem reports
- Android: problem report core, with unit tests
- Android: JNI calls for the problem report
- tests: pass the cold-stub test's asm one pointer instead of eight operands
- SPU2: V_Core::ReadInput returns silence for core 0 in bypass mode
- IopLagControl.h: include <cstddef> and spell std::size_t
- Android: the IOP thread starts on where the performance tier is two or three cores
- Linux: no ordered thread pin when the performance tier cannot hold EE, GS and VU1
- IOP thread: on by default where the performance tier is two or three cores (Qt and SDL)
- IOP thread: the GS split counts the IOP thread only where it will run
- GameDB: IOP thread for the two Korean Shadow of the Colossus releases
- IOP thread: say in the settings text when it is on, and that the game database turns it on
- Android: move the stored lag of 24576 to one frame once
- IOP thread: move a saved lag of 24576 to one frame once (Qt and SDL)
- IOP thread: Threaded needs a performance tier of at least two cores
- IOP thread: Threaded on a host whose performance tier is narrower than the threads
- IOP thread: keep an unpinned IOP thread off the performance tier when the tier is too narrow
- IOP thread: the lag bound setting defaults to one frame
- IOP thread: add the SPU2 auto-DMA stream rule to the default set
- IOP thread: default to one rule, idle with a request out; tests for the lag rules
- IOP thread: lag rules that tighten a large lag bound while the EE waits on the IOP
- IOP rec: save only the callee-saved registers IOP code writes
- tests: IOP ExecuteBlock gives back every callee-saved register
- IOP rec: keep the IOP clocks in host registers between block ends
- IOP rec: inline RAM-load fast path, no register flush on loads
- IOP rec: load RAM through a JIT-emitted stub instead of calling iopMemRead*
- tests: write the game-shaped SPU2 states to disk for tools/devlib_bench
- tests: SPU2 cold-cache cycle benchmark and a cachegrind driver
- AudioStream: poll for chunks on a timer instead of waking the worker for each one
- tests: write the SPU2 test generator's nested conditionals as if chains
- AudioStream: stop the stretch worker without draining its queue
- SPU2: write the reverb FIR resamplers in NEON directly on AArch64
- tests: freeze the reverb FIR resamplers too, and compare them directly
- SPU2: leave voices that are not playing out of the voice sum
- SPU2: interpolate the four voice taps with NEON
- tests: count branch misses in the SPU2 per-mix benchmark
- SPU2: read the two IRQ addresses once per mix instead of at every address check
- SPU2: step the ADSR envelope inline and work out the level step only on overflow
- SPU2: test the volume slide bit inline before calling V_VolumeSlide::Update
- tests: SPU2 mixer instructions-per-mix benchmark
- tests: SPU2 mixer differential test against a frozen copy of the mixer
- IOP thread: bring the IOP up to the EE when the EE stops a running SIF channel
- AudioStream: expand and time-stretch on a worker thread
- AudioStream: acquire the other end's position before reading or writing the ring
- AudioStream: tests for the ring and the stretcher, and a producer-cost benchmark
- eerunner: --frame-limiter runs a --liverun at the nominal frame rate
- IOP thread: watch what the EE does after an overshoot in idle
- IOP thread: record how late the EE takes the IOP's replies, and whether it was idle
- EE core: the event test knows it was reached through a fast-forward
- IOP thread: I2E items carry the IOP's time of production
- IOP thread: hold one SIF channel of a Lockstep skew (--iop-lockstep-skew-holds-sif0, -sif1)
- IOP thread: a Lockstep skew variant with held SIF pumps (eerunner --iop-lockstep-skew-holds)
- IOP thread: a Lockstep skew keeps the EE-to-IOP items the ring cannot hold in a spill queue
- IOP thread: count deferred SIF pumps and SBUS near-bound waits in the Threaded stats
- IOP thread: a deterministic Lockstep skew for testing (SetLockstepSkew, eerunner --iop-lockstep-skew)
- IOP thread: near bound for the EE's SBUS mailbox accesses
- IOP thread: defer EE-started SIF0/SIF1 pumps through the E2I queue (iopThreadDeferSif)
- IOP thread: raise the lag ceiling to two frames and grow the E2I ring to match
- iOS CI: key the prebuilt core cache on the macOS runner image
- Android: Load / Manage Saves lists every game's saves as one grid
- Android: on-screen controls follow a connected gamepad
- Microphone: fixes after landing the Android host microphone
- Android: host microphone input for the emulated PS2 USB mic
- USB: stop the config descriptor parser at a zero-length descriptor before reading its type
- EE rec: fuse shift pairs into one bitfield instruction
- EE rec: drop the zero test when dividing by a known constant
- EE rec: shift instead of divide by a constant power of two
- EE rec: fold the MADD accumulate into smaddl/umaddl
- EE rec: shift instead of multiply by a constant 0 or power of two
- EE rec: drop the constant write-back at fastmem and MULT/DIV sites

Full changelog: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compare/nightly-20261031...720f409f009771e5ba616a84577b783e004854c3
